plan: [I have a private value of $9. In a sealed-bid second-price auction, bidding my true value is a dominant strategy: I win when the second-highest bid is below $9 and then pay that price, yielding nonnegative surplus. Overbidding can risk paying more than my value if others bid high. With one round and independent draws, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit.]

[This is a single-round, sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values. Truthful bidding is a weakly dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds others' and pay the second-highest bid, maximizing expected surplus. No history to update beliefs. Therefore bid your private value to maximize expected profit: 20.]

[In a second-price (Vickrey) auction the dominant strategy is to bid my true private value. Bidding my value maximizes expected profit: I win exactly when the second-highest bid is below my value and pay that price. With independent draws and one round, bid truthfully to avoid overpaying or missing profitable wins.]
